evidence: Cached class data inspected as bytes and source files read/edited only. No builds, tests, syntax checks, Java class loading, game execution, process inspection, GPU commands or exports.

reference.modelSubmit: ModelFeatureRenderer$Submit.distanceToCameraSq obtains its submitted pose matrix and calls TranslucentSubmit.computeDistanceToCameraSq(Matrix4fc).
reference.distance: TranslucentSubmit reads m30/m31/m32. Mth.lengthSquared(FFF) evaluates (x*x+y*y)+z*z with float multiplies/adds. No double/FMA or actor-position reconstruction.
reference.phaseSort: TranslucentFeatureRenderPhase.sortIndices initializes 0..n-1 and calls IntArrays.unstableSort with Floats.compare(distances[b],distances[a]); sortInto emits each sorted submit with strictlyOrdered=true.
reference.fastutil: 8.5.18 comparator IntArrays.unstableSort delegates to quickSort; selection sort for length<16, median-of-nine for length>128, median-of-three pivot, equal-key partitions, range swaps and recursive partitions. Stable ties are not substituted.
reference.modelRouting: SubmitNodeCollection routes regular hasBlending models to translucentModels (phase index 7), ordinary solid models to phase index 0. Custom translucent geometry uses a separate SimpleFeatureRenderPhase at index 8. Top-level numeric orders are ascending. Outline/crumbling variants have independent routing.

port.java: AvatarDrawTarget.beginModel/endModel bracket a normal skin model, a cape model, or both wings as one submit. Individual parts keep their own transformed sinks. All-hidden skin still produces one empty batch for its submit boundary.
port.staging: Builder forbids nesting, actor transitions/open models, custom geometry inside a model, nonfinite roots, incomplete quads and resuming a model sink after its close. Model IDs are frame-local positive increasing tokens with a 2048 admission bound. Copied translation is in the packet's existing position space.
port.wire: ARCGEO08 extends each batch after render-reference metadata with strict presence u8, then if present model ID u16 and root x/y/z f32. One or fifteen bytes per batch are charged to the existing 96 MiB packet limit. Older versions decode with unknown model boundaries.
port.decode: Reject wrong presence/role, zero/oversize/out-of-order/restarted IDs, changed actor/pass or bitwise translation within a model, and nonfinite copied translations. All usual geometry/texture/frame bounds remain.
port.nativePhase: Phase.translucent_models accepts the exact frame, owning feature identity, and TranslucentModel inputs in original model order. Requires every staged SkinTranslucent model once with its original contiguous part indices, matching per-model render/prepared/consolidation/sort state, and finite explicit Java-equivalent view translations. Computes float model keys, ports the unstable sort, and emits strictly ordered PhaseOutput values for the existing dispatcher assembly.
port.planner: Plan keeps every model's part batches together in original order and on one vertex builder, independently of whether separate models may consolidate. Rejects split/restarted/late-start models and changes to their builder inputs.
port.sortingDistinction: The model sorter uses unstable whole-model distance ordering; the existing per-draw quad sorter uses stable centroid sorting with different JOML float grouping. They remain separate.

limitations: A Bedrock-emitted root in world/camera-relative space is not proven to be the Java model-submit view pose. No automatic conversion or sorting-pose equivalence is claimed; its owning producer remains missing.
This function orders the supported staged skin-model phase. Native ownership must join other participating submissions, numeric orders and phase drains; it is not a complete world phase producer.

The supported owned avatar collector now supplies its own SimpleFeatureRenderPhase HashMap traversal and retained history via ARCGEO09 (java-simple-phase-source.json). Captured Java game hashes, foreign world feature/history and optional debug shuffle remain unavailable; owned cape/wing ordering does not establish native phase ownership.
Prepared GPU equality, compatible light/material/target inputs, native world insertion and native resource lifetime ownership remain explicit independent requirements.
Outline, crumbling, ghost/alternate-target variants and complete world rendering/export parity remain unfinished.
